messages.subject: Within-between measurement invariance?
parts:
Dear Lavaan group!

We want to show that two hardware components are equal measurement instruments in regards to a psychological test, using a counterbalanced within-between subject dedign.
Is the follwing approach correct: ?

background / study design:
We want to compare two input hardware components and show that it does not influence reaction times in a psychological test.
We will have two time points of measurement and two randomly assigned groups of participants:
Group 1 will first do the test with hardware A, then with hardware B.
Group 2 will first do the test with hardware B, then with hardware A.
Significant re-test effects are to be expected.

the model:
We want to show measurement invariance, using a longitudinal MI model (as in Yu et al., 2016 http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000075).
The difference is, that we also have two independent groups (Group 1 and Group 2), so we will actually fit two longitudinal MI models (see the plot attached to this post).
Which parameters do we need to constrain to show, that hardware A and hardware B are invariant in respect to the reaction speed test?
Right now, we plan on classically constraining the parameters between group 1 and 2 (like in the code example below), and also constrain factor loadings and intercepts, but not means WITHIN the longitudinal MI models.

Thank your for your input!



some example code how it could look:
library(sem)
library(lavaan)
cfa.model <- 'Time1 =~ Indicator1_T1 + Indicator2_T1 + Indicator3_T1 + Indicator4_T1 + Indicator5_T1
              Time2 =~ Indicator1_T2 + Indicator2_T2 + Indicator3_T2 + Indicator4_T2 + Indicator5_T2
              Indicator1_T2 ~~ Indicator1_T1
              Indicator2_T2 ~~ Indicator2_T1
              Indicator3_T2 ~~ Indicator3_T1
              Indicator4_T2 ~~ Indicator4_T1
              Indicator5_T2 ~~ Indicator5_T1
              Time2 ~~ Time1'

fit_configural <- cfa(cfa.model, data = dat.col, group=c("TREATMENT"))
fit_scalar <- cfa(cfa.model, data = dat.col, group="TREATMENT", group.equal=c("loadings"))
fit_metric <- cfa(cfa.model, data = dat.col, group="TREATMENT", group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))
fit_mean <- cfa(cfa.model, data = dat.col, group="TREATMENT", group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "means"))

summary(sem::compareFit(fit_configural, fit_metric, fit_scalar, fit_mean, fit_regress))
